title: Semantic Tokens Concept
summary: Explain why semantic tokens need UI-owned authoring, stable identity, editable occurrence metadata, and local relationship reporting.
content_html:
Semantic Tokens Concept

Purpose

Let an author create and maintain structured relationships from ordinary Markdown without needing to remember or safely edit token syntax.

A token occurrence connects readable document content to a stable target:

canonical target
    -> token family + concrete target type + immutable target id
    -> editable occurrence metadata
    -> local projection and relationship report

The registered family is Catalogue. It can associate text with a Work, Series, or Moment. The author does not need to know which type is correct before searching: the UI uses the selected words to present plausible catalogue associations and the author chooses the concrete target during creation.

For nerve, that choice might be Work 00008 or Series 105. Once selected, the immutable identity includes the concrete type and id. The displayed title remains editable occurrence metadata and does not change the target.

Author Experience

The UI, not raw syntax, is the primary authoring path:

  • each family has its own source-editor toolbar action and add modal;
  • selected source text prefills the title or equivalent occurrence field;
  • discovery can search several concrete target types within that family;
  • result type, identity, and distinguishing metadata help the author choose the best association before insertion;
  • clicking inside an existing token opens its family-specific Info view;
  • identity is visible but cannot be changed through that view;
  • editable occurrence metadata can be updated and the whole token can be removed;
  • the existing local Docs Broken Links report finds unresolved semantic-token links and provides the route back to source for repair.

The source remains inspectable Markdown, but ordinary use should not depend on hand-authoring delimiters, ids, or escaped metadata.

Invariants

  • The canonical target owner remains authoritative; Docs Viewer does not copy its records into the token-definition registry.
  • Target identity is immutable after insertion. Re-targeting means remove and add.
  • The add modal is the only semantic validation gate: it confirms a current target selection, required occurrence fields, and serializable syntax.
  • Saving and rebuilding accept user-edited source as written. A malformed, unsupported, or unresolved token-like string remains ordinary text and produces neither a semantic link nor a usage-index row; a separate read-only broken-links audit may still report it.
  • Occurrence metadata is distinct from canonical target metadata.
  • Canonical and derived target data may be displayed but is not copied into the token; only occurrence-specific values are authored there.
  • The token-definition registry is configuration for supported token kinds; the derived usage index records which occurrences documents actually contain.
  • A token consumes only the named target projection declared for its kind. It does not inspect canonical records or resolve their arrays itself.
  • Usage-index attributes are rebuild-derived context, not a substitute for current occurrence fields or canonical target lookup. Preview images and similar target context are obtained by identity through the declared lookup.
  • A public document may receive an ordinary resolved anchor at build time; public readers do not resolve tokens through manage lookup or canonical data.
  • The source editor remains the only owner of buffer mutation, dirty state, saving, and rebuild.
  • Token addition and editing are manage-only.
  • Token resolution is best-effort projection, not build validation; failure to resolve a token-like string is not a build warning or error.
  • A registered family is one complete vertical capability, not just a token-definition row.
  • Generic source-editor core contains no token-definition registry or family-specific UI.
  • Core Add image and Add file continue to insert ordinary Markdown.

Catalogue entities and Tags are different semantic families. Work, Series, and Moment are concrete things an author may be referring to; Tags are abstractions used to classify or associate content. Their UI, syntax, and report meaning must not be collapsed into one generic search. Tag is not currently registered as a Semantic Tokens family.

Not This Feature

  • a public token browser or related-content report;
  • a standalone semantic-token editor or service;
  • a generic graph database or continuous validation system;
  • automatic conversion of ordinary links or media into tokens;
  • field directives, related lists, or other executable source instructions;
  • Catalogue and Tag combined into one family or discovery workflow.

The Architecture and Source Editor UI test these invariants against implementable data and interaction contracts.
